many more.
heading, level 3, WAI
The W 3C Web Accessibility Initiative (WAI) develops standards and support materials to help you
understand and implement accessibility.

heading, level 3, WCAG Evaluation Methodology (WCAG-EM) 2.0 — Note Published
link, WCAG Evaluation Methodology (WCAG-EM) 2.0, is published as a W 3C Group Note. WCAG-EM describes a
methodology with a step-by-step process to evaluate how well digital products conform to Web
Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2. WCAG-EM 1 was specifically for testing websites and web
pages. WCAG-EM 2 also applies to apps and other digital products. For an introduction to WCAG-EM,
see, link, WCAG-EM Overview, dot

heading, level 3, For Review: W 3C Accessibility Guidelines Evaluation Methodology (WCAG-EM) 2.0 — First Draft Note
link, W 3C Accessibility Guidelines Evaluation Methodology (WCAG-EM) 2.0, is available as a first Draft
Note. WCAG-EM describes a methodology with a step-by-step process to evaluate how well digital
products conform to Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2. WCAG-EM 1 is specifically for
testing websites and web pages. WCAG-EM 2 also applies to apps and other digital products. For an
introduction to WCAG-EM and more information about the WCAG-EM 2 draft, see, link, WCAG-EM Overview, dot
heading, level 3, For Review: Cognitive Accessibility Research Modules — First Draft Notes
link, Cognitive Accessibility Research Modules, are available as first Draft Notes. The documents cover
research on accessibility for people with cognitive and learning disabilities for, link, Voice Systems and
link, Conversational Interfaces, ,, link, Technology Assisted Indoor Navigation slash Wayfinding, ,, link, Online Safety and
link, Wellbeing (Algorithms and Data), , and, link, Supported Decision-Making Online, dot They address user needs,
accessibility issues, directions for solutions, and areas for further research. We particularly
seek input on what might be appropriate to add to these documents, including other relevant
research, additional user needs, and the connection between research and priorities for new work in
W 3C groups. Information on related work is in, link, Cognitive Accessibility at W 3C, dot
heading, level 3, ACT Rules Format 1.1 is a Web Standard (W 3C Recommendation)
link, Accessibility Conformance Testing (ACT) Rules Format 1.1, is now a web standard (W 3C
Recommendation). ACT Rules Format defines a format for writing accessibility test rules. The test
rules can be used for developing automated testing tools and manual testing methodologies. For an
introduction to ACT Rules, see, link, Accessibility Conformance Testing (ACT) Overview, dot

verdict.summary: This layer covers 20 criteria: 17 by deterministic rules and 17 by the trained scorer, overlapping. Other criteria are unchecked, not clean.

conformance.name: Conformance Level
conformance.establishes: Assessed 20 of 55 WCAG 2.2 A/AA success criteria.
conformance.limitation: No conformance level is claimed or established. 35 criteria were NOT assessed and are unchecked, not clean. A conforming alternate version, if this page has one, is not detected.

conformance.name: Full pages
conformance.establishes: Every structural sweep ran until the page ran out of elements, so the parts of the page a screen reader can reach were examined in full. Reach, as distinct announcements the screen reader produced against DISTINCT NAMES the browser reports — like compared with like: heading 19/19, landmark 15/13, link 40/70 of 75 on the page, graphic 3/3. A shortfall here is a coverage question about this tool, not a finding about the page.
conformance.limitation: One viewport, one state, one document. Responsive VARIATIONS each have to conform separately and only one was rendered; content inside iframes is not entered; and WCAG counts an application at a single URI as ONE page, so every state reachable without a URL change — menus, dialogs, steps of a wizard — is part of this page and was not examined. Document a529f931: served https://www.w3.org/WAI/. Render (domCensus): tabbable=78, formField=1, link=75, landmark=13, heading=19, graphic=2. THIS CAPTURE NAMED MORE THAN ONE DOCUMENT and so has no single identity — title "Search Web Accessibility Initiative (WAI) W 3C" then "How to Change Text Size or Colors Web Accessibility Initiative (WAI) W 3C". Its evidence was gathered across more than one page. Every one of the 9 form control(s) found was offered to the activation probe.

conformance.name: Complete processes
conformance.establishes: Findings are scoped to this single page.
conformance.limitation: If this page is one step of a process — signing in, checking out, completing a multi-step form — the other steps were not assessed, and WCAG conformance for the process cannot be claimed from this run. See docs/adr/0011-task-journeys.md. Third-party content (embeds, adverts, widgets) is also not distinguished from the author's own, so a finding may concern content they cannot control — the case WCAG §5.4 covers with a statement of partial conformance.

conformance.name: Only Accessibility-Supported Ways of Using Technologies
conformance.establishes: Evidence is what NVDA 2026.1.1 driving Microsoft Edge 151.0.4129.72 actually announced, so support is demonstrated rather than inferred from markup.
conformance.limitation: Accessibility support was demonstrated for that one combination only. Other screen readers, browsers and platforms behave differently and were not assessed, and one language version was read with one synthesiser — §5.5 requires each language offered to conform on its own. Nor was this page checked with the technology it relies on turned OFF or unsupported, which §5.2.5 also requires.

conformance.name: Non-Interference
conformance.establishes: Of the four criteria that apply to ALL content, assessed: 1.4.2, 2.1.2.
conformance.limitation: NOT assessed: 2.2.2, 2.3.1. These apply to all content on the page whether or not it is relied upon, so they cannot be assumed satisfied. 2.3.1 Three Flashes is visual and belongs to the rule-based layer, which ran.
